headline: Ward 6 has few chain stores because it has few stores of any kind.
summary:
Ward 6's best score and one of its worst describe the same market from two sides. Just 1.54 percent of its licensed food stores belong to one of the country's largest chains, the lowest share of any ward in Chicago. Table-service restaurants run at 1.65 per 10,000 residents, second-fewest in the city. Chains tend to open where a market already looks proven, so a ward this thin on restaurants overall will end up thin on chains too. Reporting this June backs up that picture. A Walgreens closure near 79th Street pushed the city toward a pilot program for independent pharmacies, another sign of chains pulling back rather than being crowded out by local competition.

The rest of the scorecard splits in a direction the retail story doesn't explain. Violent crime here runs at roughly 709 incidents per 10,000 residents, the worst rate of the fifty wards, and traffic injuries and the social-cohesion index both sit near the bottom too. Two more of the worst rankings, the lowest share of homes speaking a language other than English and the lowest variety of home languages spoken, draw from the same underlying share and will always move together. Building permits offer a plainer strength on their own. The city processes them here in about six and a half days, the second-fastest turnaround among the 47 wards this measure covers.
reading_the_rankings: A few of Ward 6's best rankings deserve a second look before anyone reads them as a boast. Three of the six best, on religious attendance, daily leisure time, and time poverty, were never measured inside the ward at all. They come from a national model built on demographic and circumstantial data rather than a local survey, and the group behind the model rates all three low confidence here. That's one modeled profile showing up three times under three separate labels. The parks-spending ranking needs a different kind of caution. Ward 6 tops the city in the share of aldermanic menu money spent on parks, near 44 percent, but that reflects one budget choice by the current officeholder rather than how many parks the ward has or how well they're kept.

The site identifies itself as '6th Ward Central' and names William E. Hall as alderman, with a ward office address of 8541 South State Street, Chicago, matching the office location reported elsewhere for the 6th Ward. The city's ward directory page at chicago.gov/ward6 (redirects to chicago.gov/city/en/about/wards/06.html), also fetched this session, confirms 'William E. Hall' as the 6th Ward alderperson.
